data.name: BuildEmbedded
data.value: Embedded {0}/{1} chunks ({2}/s, ~{3} min left)
data.comment: The line a person actually watches: it prints once per completed batch, which is roughly every fifteen seconds, and on a hook run it is the only progress there is. 2 and 3 arrive already formatted to one decimal, invariantly, so a Russian machine writes 10.2 rather than 10,2. One line in both languages, same four facts in the same order: two would put the count and its estimate on different lines, which is where a reader loses the pairing.

data.name: GenerationNotPublishedFact
data.value: No index generation is published for this repository.
data.comment: localai sync and --root are typed, so they stay as they are; {0} is a path and never moves. The command that repairs this lives in the matching Remedy key, and IndexText joins the two back with a single space for every caller that prints the whole sentence - so what this product has always printed is byte-identical. A caller that knows a build already holds the sync gate prints this half alone, because a second localai sync exits 75 sync_busy and the block that stands where the command was says so instead.

data.name: EmbeddingBrokerNotStarted
data.value: The LocalAi broker did not start in time. {0}
data.comment: {0} is BrokerBootstrapException's own diagnostic - phase and last observation - which is English in every language because BrokerProcess has no catalogue of its own. It restates this sentence in English, and that duplication goes away when those messages are catalogued rather than by dropping this one: dropping it is the defect #393 names.

data.name: EmbeddingBackendUnavailable
data.value: Ollama is not available, so the embedding job for model '{0}' did not finish. {1}
data.comment: Ollama by name, because it is the only transport and the only thing the reader can act on. {0} is the embedding model id and is never translated. {1} is BrokerJobFailedException's message, already catalogued and already cut to 200 characters, so the job id and the marker before Ollama's own words come with it - do not re-derive them from FailureReason.

data.name: BuildEmbeddingStopped
data.value: Embedding stopped at {0} of {1} chunks. What is embedded is saved — running this build again continues from there.
data.comment: The count is what #389 was filed for, and the second clause is the fact that makes running it again cheap. Both holes are counts and stay invariant. Said only where an embedding checkpoint is configured, and understated by construction: SaveBatch runs before done is incremented, and the halving path saves more, so what the checkpoint holds is never less than what this claims.

data.name: BuildEmbeddingStoppedAtStart
data.value: None of the {0} chunks were embedded.
data.comment: No remedy clause: nothing was finished, so there is nothing to tell the reader is kept.

data.name: RoslynLoading
data.value: Loading C# from '{0}'. Restoring dependencies first — up to {1} min.
data.comment: Said before the wait, not after it: a line printed once the restore is over explains a silence the reader has already sat through. {1} is the same constant the restore actually waits on, passed in rather than written twice, so the sentence cannot drift from the timeout it describes.

data.name: RoslynRestored
data.value: Dependencies restored in {0}s. Opening the projects.
data.comment: Printed only when the restore process exited 0. The failure and timeout paths print their own diagnostics, so a run that shows the loading line, then a failure, and no restored line is telling the truth.

data.name: RoslynOpened
data.value: Opened {0} projects in {1}s.
data.comment: The count is honest only after the call - MSBuildWorkspace.OpenSolutionAsync is one opaque operation with no per-project callback, so this is the first moment the number exists. Both holes are invariant.

data.name: SemanticOverlayNotBuiltFact
data.value: This worktree has no semantic overlay for generation '{0}', so no stale or mixed result was returned.
data.comment: The ordinary state of an edited or unsynced worktree, not a fault: what is absent is the worktree's overlay, not generation '{0}'s semantic.sidx, which loaded a line earlier. Reported as SemanticIndexUnreadable until #409, which is why an everyday edit read as a corrupt index. The closing clause is OverlayMissing's, to the byte, in both languages - the same fact on the search path, and one spelling per concept. It stays true here too: the overlay load throws rather than materialising anything, and the heuristic locations that follow are computed live and tagged Heuristic. The command that repairs this lives in the matching Remedy key, and IndexText joins the two back with a single space; a caller that knows a build already holds the sync gate prints this half alone, because a second localai sync exits 75 sync_busy.

data.name: SemanticOverlayNotBuiltRemedy
data.value: Build one: localai sync --root {0}
data.comment: Build one, not Rebuild it: nothing exists to rebuild. The same words as GenerationNotPublishedRemedy for the same shape of state, in a key of its own so that rewording either cannot move the other.

data.name: SemanticOverlayUnreadableFact
data.value: The semantic overlay for this worktree could not be read.
data.comment: An overlay that is present and will not load - InvalidDataException from SemanticIndexOverlay.Load or Materialize, a sharing violation, a denied read. Rare, and a real fault. It names the worktree rather than the generation, because the file that failed is the worktree's and the working root is in the matching Remedy. The cause is the InnerException, as with SemanticIndexUnreadableFact.

data.name: SemanticOverlayUnreadableRemedy
data.value: Rebuild it: localai sync --root {0}
data.comment: The same words as SemanticIndexUnreadableRemedy, in a key of its own: the two states repair identically today and are free to diverge without dragging each other.
